title: 🎓 The US First Lady promotes the "Superintelligence" challenge for school students — registration open until December 18!
body: 🎓 The US First Lady promotes the "Superintelligence" challenge for school students — registration open until December 18!

First Lady Melania Trump promoted the "Presidential AI Challenge 2027" in an interview on Fox Business on Friday, November 20, for school students from kindergarten through grade 12, and teachers and schools across America.
The challenge is team-based: students build projects with superintelligence tools to solve real problems in their schools and communities.
Registration is open now via the "AI.gov" website and closes on December 18, 2026, and schools have until April 30, 2027 to complete the readiness stages.
Participating schools can earn the "First Lady's Seal for AI Readiness", and the winners are invited to the White House to receive an award.

More than 20,000 students from all fifty states, Puerto Rico, Washington and 49 Department of Defense schools in 10 countries took part in the first edition of the challenge, with more than 2,500 projects.

The challenge was announced from the White House in October, and it is part of a federal policy: an executive order on September 29, 2026 directing all agencies to call artificial intelligence "superintelligence" in official correspondence.
Melania said she uses AI herself for research, but "we must be vigilant and not believe everything" AI agents and language models tell us.
Simply put: imagine a national competition in which pupils build AI projects that solve their schools' problems, and the winners are honoured at the White House. That is the idea of the challenge.
Would you like our schools to take part in AI challenges like this one?
